standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the projection p : Y -> X proper as the composite of the closed immersion Y -> P^1_X with the proper projection P^1_X -> X; this is assertion (1).

standard_prerequisites.name: Pullback of an effective Cartier divisor along a morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, labels divisors-definition-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisor (statement, proof line 2716) and divisors-lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined (proof line 2756)
standard_prerequisites.use: Defines Y_0 and Y_infty as pullbacks of the two standard sections and supplies the local criterion that makes them defined because q(eta') avoids D_0 and D_infty; assertions (3) and the dimension count following it are built on this.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dimension of the support of a divisor and compatibility of pushforward with divisors of rational functions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-divisor-delta-dimension (proof line 2759), lemma-cycle-push-sheaf (proof line 2790) and lemma-proper-pushforward-alteration (proof line 2794)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the delta-dimension of Y_0 and Y_infty, identifies p_*[Y_0]_{n-1} with the class of the image of Y_0, and supplies the compatibility of p_* with div(f) that yields assertion (5).

core_obligations: Identify Y independent of the chosen open U as the closure of the single point (1, f)(eta) over the generic point eta of X, and record that Y is integral with (1, f)(U) as a dense open subscheme (proof lines 2733-2740).

Prove the structural assertions (1), (2) and (3) together with dim_delta(Y) = n and dim_delta(Y_0) = dim_delta(Y_infty) = n - 1: properness by composition of proper morphisms, the isomorphism over U because Y meets U times_S P^1_S in the graph, and definiteness of the pullbacks because q(eta') = f(eta) is not in D_0 or D_infty as f is invertible (proof lines 2742-2759).

Establish assertion (4): at a point xi of Y_0 the local equation is f, so the coefficient of an integral Z of dimension n - 1 in div_Y(f) equals length_{O_{Y,xi}}(O_{Y_0,xi}), which is exactly its coefficient in [Y_0]_{n-1}, and the same argument with 1/f handles the negative coefficients coming from Y_infty (proof lines 2761-2778).

Establish assertions (5) and (6): Y_0 sits inside the graph of the zero section so Y_0 -> X is a closed immersion with p_* O_{Y_0} = O_{Y'_0}, whence p_*[Y_0]_{n-1} = [Y'_0]_{n-1} by the pushforward of cycle classes, and the same for Y_infty; assertion (5) itself follows from compatibility of p_* with div(f) (proof lines 2780-2794).
proof_roadmap: Identify Y as the closure of the graph of the generic point and note it is integral (proof lines 2733-2740).
Prove properness, the isomorphism over U, definiteness of the two pullback divisors and their dimensions (proof lines 2742-2759).
Compare coefficients to get div_Y(f) = [Y_0]_{n-1} - [Y_infty]_{n-1}, then push forward and identify the images to obtain the two divisor descriptions on X (proof lines 2761-2794).
difficulty_reason: The lemma packages the standard construction attached to a rational function on an integral X of delta-dimension n: the closure Y of its graph in X times_S P^1_S is proper over X, is an isomorphism over the open set where f is invertible, the two pullbacks of the standard sections are defined, and the divisor of f on Y and on X is the difference of the two cycle classes (statement lines 2700-2731, tag 02RQ). The proof combines four ingredients that are not the lemma itself: properness by composition, definiteness of the pullback divisors via the generic point, a coefficient-by-coefficient comparison of the order of f against the length of the local ring of Y_0, and the identification of the pushforwards of the two cycle classes through assertion (5). The coefficient comparison is the substantive part, so the claim is H2.
